title: Gold's 17% Jump: What's Driving It & Fed Rate Cut Impact?
description: Gold prices have surged by 17% from their June lows, showcasing resilience amidst global market dynamics. This rally is primarily driven by geopolitical uncer.

faq.q: Why are gold prices rising even with potential Fed rate hikes?
faq.a: Gold prices are rising due to multiple factors like geopolitical tensions, inflation hedging demand, and strong central bank buying, which are currently outweighing the dampening effect of potential interest rate increases.

faq.q: What is the significance of the $4620-$4630 per ounce hurdle for COMEX gold?
faq.a: This range represents a significant resistance level identified by experts. If gold prices break above this, it could signal further upward momentum; otherwise, it might lead to a period of consolidation or correction.

faq.q: How do Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) differ from Gold ETFs?
faq.a: SGBs are government securities offering an annual interest payment and tax exemption on capital gains at maturity for individuals. Gold ETFs are units representing physical gold, traded on exchanges, offering liquidity but without interest payments or maturity tax exemption.

faq.q: Is physical gold still a good investment option?
faq.a: While culturally significant, physical gold comes with storage risks, making charges, and potential purity issues. Financial instruments like SGBs and Gold ETFs offer more convenient, secure, and often more cost-effective ways to invest in gold for financial returns.

faq.q: What are the tax implications of investing in gold in India?
faq.a: Capital gains from Gold ETFs and physical gold are taxed as Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) if held for less than 3 years, or Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) with indexation if held for more than 3 years. For SGBs, capital gains are exempt from tax for individual investors if held till maturity (8 years). Interest from SGBs is taxable at the investor's slab rate.

based_on.title: Gold shines, braving odds, rises 17% from June lows — What’s behind the jump? Will it impact Fed rate cut decision?

fact_check.summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of gold investment in India, but contains several inaccuracies regarding the taxation of gold ETFs, physical gold, and SGBs, particularly concerning holding periods and tax rates.

corrections.note: Corrected tax implications for Gold ETFs and Sovereign Gold Bonds regarding holding periods and tax rates, removing outdated information about indexation benefits for Gold ETFs and clarifying SGB tax exemption conditions.

edits.why: For Gold ETFs, STCG applies if held for 12 months or less (taxed at slab rate), and LTCG applies if held for more than 12 months (taxed at 12.5% without indexation). The 3-year holding period and 20% tax with indexation are not applicable to Gold ETFs as per recent tax changes.

Capital gains on SGBs are exempt at maturity for original subscribers. If sold before maturity, LTCG is taxed at 20% with indexation if held for more than 3 years, or at 12.5% without indexation if held for more than 12 months but less than 3 years. The tax exemption at maturity is strictly for original subscribers who hold the bonds continuously.

For Gold ETFs, STCG applies if held for 12 months or less (taxed at slab rate), and LTCG applies if held for more than 12 months (taxed at 12.5% without indexation). For physical gold, STCG applies if held for 24 months or less (taxed at slab rate), and LTCG applies if held for more than 24 months (taxed at 12.5% without indexation). The 3-year holding period for LTCG with indexation is generally not applicable to Gold ETFs or physical gold as per recent tax changes.
